LESSON GOALS
•	 To understand simple stories and conversations.
•	 To give and follow simple directions and instructions.
•	 To ask and answer questions about familiar topics 
(personal information, clothes, colours, weather, etc.).
•	 To talk about things you can see in different places 
in the world and things you can buy or do in a shop.
MATERIALS
•	 TR#12 The Toyshop Song
•	 TR#13 Directions Song
•	 TR#20 Time to Go Home 
•	 After-School Activities (P.E.M.2)
•	 Days of the Week cards (P.E.M.5)
•	 Teacher materials for Act. 3: A3 map (P.2.3) + Item 
memory cards (P.2.3) + bike cutout
•	 Teacher materials for Act. 5: Shopping List cards and 
Shop cards (P.2.5)
•	 Teacher materials for Act. 9: Number cards (P.E.M.3) 
•	 Teacher materials for Act. 1: Characters and Places 
(P.2.1)
•	 Teacher materials for Act. 6: Shop cards (P.2.5) + ball
•	 Big Book
•	 Shops and Items (A3) and Transport playing cards (P.S2)
•	 Crayons or pencils
•	 Day 6 Stickers (1 per child)
BEFORE CLASS
Bring your notes with the storytelling variables chosen last

LESSON PLAN

2.– ACTIVITY 7: DIRECTIONS SONG (TR#13) (4’)
> Main activity
To perform the song, have the Ss stand with their back against 
the wall in a line, side by side. Then the first time they sing the 
song they will simply turn left and right while standing in place 
and then walk straight ahead when the song says to do so.
The second time you do the activity, they must line up behind 
one another forming a train, holding onto the shoulders of the 
S in front of them. Then, this time, when the song says turn left 
and right, they will actually walk around the room while doing 
so. The song will speed up so make sure the Ss are ready to 
do the actions quickly.
DIRECTIONS SONG
Turn left, left, left
Turn right, right, right
Walk straight ahead
Straight, straight, straight
That was great! Now line up! Ready? Steady? Go! 
Turn left, left, left
Turn right, right, right
Walk straight ahead
Straight, straight, straight
(repeat) 
Very good! Now let’s go faster!
Turn left, left, left
Turn right, right, right
Walk straight ahead
Straight, straight, straight
(repeat)
3.– STUDENT STORYTELLING WITH CHANGES (PP.8-14) 
(9’)
Have your students tell the second half of the story using the 
variables from last week. Please see the section on storytelling 
in the Warm-Up Routines Index.

4.– WORKSHEET: WHERE CAN YOU BUY THESE? (P.9) 
(9’)
Where Can You Buy These?
CAT
FOOD
9
NOTE: if you collected your Ss books during the booklet 
activity, have them ask you for it now by saying “Can I have 
my book please?”; otherwise, ask them to take it out of their 
bag. Explain the activity before giving out the books/asking Ss 
to take them out since they might get distracted.
MATERIALS
•	 Crayons or pencils
This worksheet consists of a grid with different shops and a 
selection of items. The students must take it in turns to ask each 
other questions to identify what can be bought at each shop.
Model the task by pointing to the ice cream parlour and 
asking, “What can you buy at the ice cream parlour?”. The 
group should answer, “You can buy ice cream at the ice cream 
parlour.”. Now drag your finger down the page from the ice 
cream parlour until you reach the square in line with the ice 
cream. Show Ss they must draw a tick in the box.
Continue the activity by having the Ss take on the teacher 
role. Ss will ask the S to their left, “What can you buy at the 
bakery?”, and the S must respond, “You can buy croissants at 
the bakery.”. Then the group should tick the corresponding box. 
Repeat these steps until you finish the worksheet or time is up.
KEY
Ice cream parlour: ice cream
Bakery: croissants
Pet shop: cat food
Clothes shop: trousers
Café: fizzy drinks
Butcher’s: meat
Bookshop: books
Fishmonger’s: fish
Toyshop: video games
Greengrocer’s: tomatoes

> Advanced Groups
If you feel like your Ss are familiar with the language and 
understand the worksheet dynamics, you can have them work 
in pairs by asking and answering the questions above.

6.– ACTIVITY 3: CAN YOU TELL ME THE WAY? (9’)
P.2.3
P.2.3
TARGET LANGUAGE
Turn right
Go past
Go straight ahead
Turn left
Behind
On your right
On your left
Opposite
Next to
Between
> How to Play
In this game, the Ss must tell their classmate the correct 
way to get to the shop to buy a certain item.

> Warm-Up
Quickly review the name of the items (P.2.3) with the Ss 
and where they can buy them. Ask, “Where can you buy a 
dress?” to which they should answer, “You can buy a dress at 
the clothes shop.” If needed, review the shops on the A3 that 
your Ss find tricky (such as charity shop, town hall, dentist, 
basketball court, football pitch, etc.)
NOTE: if your Ss are familiar with the target language, you 
may skip this step.
> Main Activity
Pair the Ss up (S1 and S2). Put the Item memory cards (P.2.3) 
face down on the table. To do the activity, proceed as detailed 
below. We highly encourage you to model the steps with a S 
first. Say, “Let’s go explore the city!”. Then proceed as follows: 
•	 S1: Takes a bike cutout and turns over an item card.
•	 T: “What do you need to buy?”
•	 S1: “I need to buy dog food.” (or whatever item is on 
the card). 
•	 T: “Where can you buy dog food?”
•	 S2: “You can buy dog food at the pet shop.”
•	 T: “S1, you are at the bookshop.”
•	 S1: “Can you tell me the way (to the pet shop), please?”
•	 S2: Gives directions accordingly. For example: “To get 
to the pet shop, turn right. Go straight ahead and go 
past the supermarket and the sports centre. At the 
sports centre turn left. You will find the pet shop on 
your right / the pet shop is opposite the charity shop.”
> Follow-Up
Ask Ss about the location of different shops. For example: 
“John, where is the greengrocer’s?” to which they should reply, 
“The greengrocer’s is between the bakery and the charity 
shop.”
7.– ACTIVITY 5: SHOPPING LISTS (VERSION 1) (8’)
P.2.5
P.2.5

> How to Play
In this game, Ss need to find three shops where they can 
buy the items on their shopping list. To do so, they will have to 
ask other Ss questions to find out who has the shop they need. 
> Warm-Up
Go over the items that can be bought at the shops using the 
Shopping Lists cards (P.2.5). Ask them, for example, “Where 
can you buy boots?” to which Ss must answer, “You can buy 
boots at the shoe shop.” 
NOTE: if your Ss are familiar with the target language, you 
may skip this step.
> Main Activity
Introduce the activity by saying, “It’s time to go shopping! 
Let’s see if you can buy all the items on your shopping list!”. 
Give one Shopping List card (P.2.5) to each S. The Ss should 
keep their shopping lists face up on the table in front of them. 
Shuffle the Shop cards (P.2.5) which depict the different shops 
and give three cards to each S. Make sure that the Ss don’t 
show their cards to their classmates.
Place the remaining cards face down in a pile in the middle 
of the table.
Ss should take it in turns to ask other Ss if they have a shop 
they need. For example, “Jane, have you got the ice cream 
parlour?”. If Jane has got the card, she should answer, “Yes, I 
have. Here you are.” and give it to her classmate. If Jane hasn’t 
got the card she should say, “No, I haven’t. Take a card.” and the 
other S must pick up a card from the deck in middle of the table. 
When Ss find the correct shop for an item on their list, they 
must always say, “You can buy ... at the...”
The game finishes when you have run out of time, or when 
a S has completed their shopping list.
> Follow-Up
Ask the two Ss who finished first to describe their shopping 
list as follows:
•	 You can buy tomatoes at the greengrocer’s.
•	 You can buy boots at the shoe shop.
•	 You can buy fish at the fishmonger’s.

8.– ACTIVITY 9: NUMBERS (VERSION 2) (6’)
P.E.M.3
55
This game is based on the traditional game Snap! 
Mix the numbers (P.E.M.3.) with the jokers by getting the Ss 
to say, “Mix, mix, mix” and encouraging them to say “Stop!”
Take the whole deck and start turning over the cards and 
putting them in the middle. The Ss should state whatever number 
comes out by saying, for example, “It’s number 62.”. Whenever 
a joker is turned over, they should say, “Snap!”. Try to keep a 
good pace so that the game is more interesting. 
The first S to say, “Snap!” gets all the cards in the middle, and 
the next round starts. The game is over when it’s not possible 
to put more cards in the middle. The winner is the S with the 
most cards.

10.– TIME TO GO HOME (TR#20) (2’) 
Sing the Time to Go Home song and have the Ss form a line 
before leaving the class.
BONUS
ACTIVITY 1: CHARACTER MATCHING
P.2.1
P.2.1
> Warm-Up
Quickly review the actions that each character is doing by 
putting the Place cards (P.2.1) down on the table. Say, “Grandpa 
and Grandma are going to the doctor’s, Mum is going to the 
hairdresser’s, and Dad is doing the gardening.”
Show the Ss the X cards and ask, “Why can’t Mum take 
Pam and Paul to the toyshop?”, to which they should reply, 
“Because she is going to the hairdresser’s.” Continue in this 
manner until you have gone over all the pairs.
NOTE: if your Ss are familiar with the target language, you 
may skip this step.
> Main Activity
To introduce the activity, say, “Let’s see if you remember 
what Pam and Paul’s family are doing!”. Put the P.2.1 cards 
in two piles face down: X cards on one side, Place cards on 
the other. The Ss must flip a card from each pile to match the 
character with the correct reason for them to not be able to 
take Pam and Paul to the toyshop.
If they have a match, they should say, “Mum can’t take 
Pam and Paul to the toyshop, because she is going to the 
hairdresser’s. I’ve got a pair!” If they don’t, they should say 
“I’ve got Grandpa and Grandma and doing the gardening; it’s 
not a pair, what a shame!”
> Correct matches and structures
•	 Mum + going to the hairdresser’s: “Mum (she) can’t take 
Pam and Paul to the toyshop because she is going to 
the hairdresser’s.”

•	 Dad + doing the gardening: “Dad (he) can’t take Pam and 
Paul to the toyshop because he is doing the gardening.” 
•	 Grandma and Grandpa + going to the doctor’s: “Grandma 
and Grandpa (they) can’t take Pam and Paul to the 
toyshop because they are going to the doctor’s.” 
> Follow-Up
Quickly split the group into two teams. Show team A the X 
card and team B the matching place card. Each team should 
say the part of the structure corresponding to their card. For 
example:
•	 Team A: “Grandpa and Grandma can’t take Pam and 
Paul to the toyshop...”
•	 Team B: “...because they are going to the doctor’s.”
ACTIVITY 6: FREEZE!
P.2.5
> Main Activity
The Ss sit on the floor in a circle. Tell them, “Let’s see if 
you remember what you can buy at each shop!”. Place the 
pile of Shop cards (P.2.5) face down in the middle of the circle 
and get the Ss to begin passing the ball. Tell them that when 
you say “Freeze!”, they must stop. Whenever you feel like it, 
shout out “FREEZE!” and the S holding the ball must pick up 
a card from the middle of the circle and answer the question, 
“What can you buy at the…?” as quickly as possible. Once Ss 
are used to the game you can make it more dynamic by not 
asking them the question and letting them come up with the 
sentence themselves. For example:
•	 You can buy jumpers at the clothes shop.
•	 You can buy video games at the toy shop.
•	 You can buy muffins at the bakery.
NOTE: you can also play songs from the story to make it 
more dynamic. You can still say “Freeze!” every time you pause 
the song.
